ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a square, and all the gray regions extend outward from the common vertex at the lower-left corner of the square. There is a gray triangular region on the left side, whose outer side corresponds to distance a on the top side; the gray region in the upper-right corner can be regarded as consisting of two triangles corresponding to distance b on the top side and distance c on the right side; there is a gray triangular region on the lower right, whose outer side corresponds to distance d on the right side. The problem gives that the area of the square is 36, and the sum of the areas of all gray parts is 27. Reasoning: The area of the square is 36, so the side length is 6. The base of each gray triangle is on the top side or the right side of the square, and the other common vertex is the lower-left corner. If the base is on the top side, then the height to the base is the side length of the square, 6; if the base is on the right side, then the height to the base is also the side length of the square, 6. Therefore the total gray area is (1/2)×6×(a+b+c+d)=3(a+b+c+d). It is known that the total gray area is 27, so 3(a+b+c+d)=27, giving a+b+c+d=9.

method.method_draft: Direct grey-area decomposition. From the diagram, read that all grey regions are fan-shaped with a common vertex at the bottom-left corner of the square. Their outer bases lie on the top or right side of the square: the left grey wedge has base a on the top side, the upper-right grey corner region can be split into two triangles with bases b on the top side and c on the right side, and the lower-right grey wedge has base d on the right side. From the text, the square has area 36, so its side length is 6. Each such triangle has height 6, because its base is on the top or right side and the opposite vertex is the bottom-left corner. Therefore the total grey area is (1/2)·6·(a+b+c+d)=3(a+b+c+d). Set this equal to the given grey area 27 and solve a+b+c+d=9.

method.method_draft: Complementary white-area route. From the diagram, read that the rays from the bottom-left corner partition the square into alternating grey and white wedges, and that the labeled grey boundary lengths a, b, c, and d occupy parts of the top and right sides. The remaining unlabeled portions of the top and right sides are exactly the bases of the white wedges. From the text, the square area is 36, so the side length is 6 and the combined length of the top and right sides is 12. Let S=a+b+c+d. Then the total base length of the white wedges is 12-S.
